stem.en: "Journey to the End of the Earth" was written by

explanation.en: Tishani Doshi wrote this travel account.

stem.en: The author travelled to Antarctica aboard

options.en: a cruise liner from Cape Town
the Russian research vessel Akademik Shokalskiy

explanation.en: She sailed on the Russian research vessel Akademik Shokalskiy.

stem.en: Where did the author's journey begin?

explanation.en: It began in Madras, now Chennai.

stem.en: What feeling did Antarctica's landscape create in the author?

options.en: a sense of how small and recent humans are

explanation.en: The vastness made her aware of humanity's smallness and short history.

stem.en: Gondwana was

explanation.en: Gondwana was a giant southern supercontinent.

stem.en: Gondwana was centred roughly around

explanation.en: It was centred roughly around present-day Antarctica.

stem.en: When did the Gondwana landmass break up into separate countries, according to the account?

options.en: only in the last thousand years
after the dinosaurs were wiped out and the age of mammals began

explanation.en: The account links the separation to the period after the dinosaurs' extinction.

stem.en: Why do scientists study Antarctica's ice layers?

options.en: because they trap ancient air and carbon that reveal past climate

explanation.en: Trapped carbon and air show how the climate has changed over time.

stem.en: Phytoplankton are

explanation.en: They are microscopic single-celled plants in the sea.

stem.en: What do phytoplankton do with the sun's energy?

explanation.en: They absorb carbon and supply oxygen.

stem.en: According to the account, further depletion of the ozone layer would

options.en: harm phytoplankton and so the food chain and carbon cycle
have no effect on the ocean

explanation.en: Damage to phytoplankton would spread through the food chain and carbon cycle.

stem.en: The lesson the author draws from phytoplankton is that

options.en: Antarctica is too far to matter
looking after small things helps the bigger things take care of themselves

explanation.en: Caring for small things protects the larger system.

stem.en: Who leads the Students on Ice programme?

explanation.en: Geoff Green, a Canadian, leads the programme.

stem.en: What is the main aim of Students on Ice?

options.en: to give young people understanding of and respect for the planet
to set up schools in Antarctica

explanation.en: It aims to build understanding and respect for the planet.

stem.en: Why are students chosen for the expedition?

options.en: Adults are not allowed in Antarctica
They are at an age to absorb, learn and act
They can stand the cold better

explanation.en: Green believes young people absorb, learn and act.

stem.en: Which of these is NOT a theme of "Journey to the End of the Earth"?

options.en: the role of young people in saving the planet

explanation.en: Untouchability is a theme of Bama's memoir, not this account.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Antarctica is an important place to study the history of the earth's climate.
Reason (R): Its layers of ice have trapped carbon and air from hundreds of thousands of years ago.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: The trapped records in the ice are exactly why it is valuable for climate history.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Phytoplankton are large animals at the top of the Southern Ocean food chain.
Reason (R): Phytoplankton use the sun's energy to absorb carbon and supply oxygen.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: A is false: they are tiny single-celled plants at the base of the food chain. R is true.

stem.en: What trend does the data show?

options.en: Sea ice rose and then fell
Sea ice is decreasing every year
Sea ice is increasing every year

explanation.en: Each year the area is smaller than the year before.

passage.en: A school eco-club measured the area of sea ice near a research station in the same month over four years: 2019: 12.0 lakh sq km, 2020: 11.4 lakh sq km, 2021: 10.9 lakh sq km, 2022: 10.1 lakh sq km. The club also noted fewer krill, the small creatures that feed on phytoplankton and are eaten by penguins and whales.

stem.en: Why might fewer krill worry the club, in light of the account?

options.en: Krill link phytoplankton to penguins and whales, so the whole food chain is affected
Krill produce all the world's oxygen
Krill are not part of any food chain

explanation.en: A break at one link of the chain affects animals higher up.

passage.en: A school eco-club measured the area of sea ice near a research station in the same month over four years: 2019: 12.0 lakh sq km, 2020: 11.4 lakh sq km, 2021: 10.9 lakh sq km, 2022: 10.1 lakh sq km. The club also noted fewer krill, the small creatures that feed on phytoplankton and are eaten by penguins and whales.

stem.en: Arrange in order: (i) the age of mammals begins (ii) Gondwana exists, centred near Antarctica (iii) Antarctica becomes a vast ice-covered continent (iv) the dinosaurs are wiped out

explanation.en: Gondwana, dinosaurs wiped out, mammals rise, then today's icy Antarctica.

stem.en: Match: (i) Geoff Green (ii) Akademik Shokalskiy (iii) phytoplankton (iv) Gondwana - (a) ancient supercontinent (b) leader of Students on Ice (c) Russian research vessel (d) single-celled plants

explanation.en: Each item matches its description.

stem.en: "Journey to the End of the Earth" is best described as

options.en: a short story with a twist ending
a non-fiction travelogue with an environmental message

explanation.en: It is a non-fiction travel account carrying a message about climate change.
